@vitor-mariano if I understand your comment correctly this happens only with the single input `Run` shorthand due to a bug with how form widths / input widths are handled? In that case, we'd be more than delighted to accept a PR for the fix but also happy to fix it ourselves as it seems it's an issue with how the theme/width is being applied.

Not really. Let me detail it more.

1. The problems happen regardless of the standalone use. I just emphasized that a standalone input works similarly to a grouped input.
2. I checked the problems with `WithWidth` happen to other field types.
3. The panic is only one bug related to `WithWidth`.

Fixing the panic issue, I noticed a second bug. The lib ignores the width of the fields. This happens in two scenarios:
1. When you also set `WithWidth` in `form`, it overrides the width of all its children.
    ``` go
    huh.NewForm(
	    huh.NewGroup(
		    huh.NewInput().
			    Title("Enter Slack workspace name").
			    Value(&workspace).
			    Description("Blah").
			    WithWidth(40),
	    ),
    ).WithWidth(60).Run()
    ```
    The resulting size will be 60 because `form` propagates `WithWidth` to all its children.
2. When you don't set `WithWidth` in `form` it propagates the window size to all its children, similarly to when you set `WithWidth` explicitly:
    https://github.com/charmbracelet/huh/blob/main/form.go#L325-L331 
    ``` go
    case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
	    if f.width > 0 {
		    break
	    }
	    for _, group := range f.groups {
		    group.WithWidth(msg.Width)
	    }
    ```

I haven't tested groups yet, but I'm pretty sure the same bug applies.

I think the solution is to have two properties in all field types:
1. `maxWidth` that holds the desired field width.
2. the existing `width` will be the current rendered width.

To handle these properties, we could have the following functions:
1. A new function `Resize(width int)` will set the current width without changing the `maxWidth`.
2. The existing `WithWidth(width int)` function will set the `maxWidth` and resize.

This way, the form and groups can control the current width of its fields respecting the maximum width set by the developer.

Btw, the magic color \#00020A is the reverse (or complementary) color of a given hex color \#FFFDF5.

Given hex color: \#FFFDF5

1. Convert \#FFFDF5 to RGB:
   - Red (R): FF (hex) = 255 (decimal)
   - Green (G): FD (hex) = 253 (decimal)
   - Blue (B): F5 (hex) = 245 (decimal)

2. Subtract each component from 255:
   - Red: \(255 - 255 = 0\)
   - Green: \(255 - 253 = 2\)
   - Blue: \(255 - 245 = 10\)

3. Convert the results back to hex:
   - Red: \(0\) (decimal) = \(00\) (hex)
   - Green: \(2\) (decimal) = \(02\) (hex)
   - Blue: \(10\) (decimal) = \(0A\) (hex)

So, the reverse color of \#FFFDF5 is \#00020A.

I encountered this issue on Windows using several bubbletea models in sequence that solicited input from the user, but I think my findings are relevant to this issue. After my first bubbletea program returned and my second bubbletea program started, it ignored the first key press.

What I found was that the read loop on Windows blocks on [this line](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/blob/main/key_windows.go#L28) until it reads console input. Upon shutting down the bubbletea program, its `shutdown` method is called, which calls the input reader's `Cancel` method. On Windows, this sends a [CancelIo](https://github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea/blob/main/inputreader_windows.go#L60) syscall.

My expectation is that the blocked call in the read loop would unblock and the goroutine would exit. After spending some time with a debugger, I found this isn't the case. When my second bubbletea program initializes, it spins up its own read loop. But the very next key press is read by the first program's input reader. The first key press appears to be ignored by my second program because it never receives it, though it receives all following key presses.

Interestingly, the [CancelIo docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/cancelio) read:
> The function does not cancel I/O operations that other threads issue for a file handle.

Since the read loop is in its own goroutine, separate from the `windows.CancelIo` call, I suspect bubbletea is using the wrong function. My app works as expected if I set `runtime.GOMAXPROCS(1)`, which somewhat confirms my suspicion. When I have more time to devote to this, I'll see if the fix is as simple as using `windows.CancelIoEx` instead of `windows.CancelIo`.

The form height is calculated when the terminal size is received and is never recalculated afterwards, so a group whose content grows - a dynamic description that needs more lines - keeps the old height and the new lines are cut off by the group's viewport.
